newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-RIO TEAMS HOLD "BLACK PROTEST" BEFORE MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RIO TEAMS HOLD "BLACK PROTEST" BEFORE MATCH.

text.p: Flamengo and Fluminense took the field for their derby match on Sunday wearing black shirts over their regular strips in protest at the chaotic organisation of the Rio de Janeiro championship.
Botafogo, another leading Rio team, did the same before their game against Madureira on Saturday.
Fans also joined, waving banners demanding the resignation of Eduardo Viana, president of the Rio de Janeiro federation, who has been blamed for much of the chaos.
The tournament has been marked by a series of confusions but the last straw was the hotly-disputed refereeing in last Wednesday's game between Vasco da Gama and Volta Redonda.
Vasco won 2-1 after scoring their goals in the fourth and sixth minute of injury time which had been controversially added on by referee Carlos Duque.
Volta Redonda also had two players sent off in the second half but claimed both decisions were severe. Far from celebrating their team's win, Vasco fans changed "robbery" and "it's a fix."
But on Sunday Viana was defiant: "I will only leave the presidency dead," he claimed.
On the field, Fluminense won 3-2 despite having half their regular team missing through injury or suspension.

Brazil international Romario scored a penalty and a spectacular individual goal to give Flamengo a 2-1 lead but Brazil's best supported team fell apart after having Fabio Baianio and Fabiano sent off in the second half.
Botafogo, who won the first stage of the tournament, lead the second stage despite drawing 0-0.

The competition is divided into three preliminary stages with the winners meeting in a play-off, though numerous complications arise if the same team wins more than one stage or if teams finish the final play-off level on points.

Sao Paulo's Colombian striker Victor Hugo Aristizabal scored a goal, missed a penalty and was then sent off -- seemingly unfairly -- in his team's 2-0 win over Botafogo-Ribeirao Preto in the Sao Paulo championship.
Aristizabal appeared to be the victim when he was struck in the face by Botafogo defender Gustavo just before halftime but both players were shown the red card.
Sao Paulo's Adriano and Botafogo's Valdeir were also dismissed in the second half as both teams finished with nine men.

Palmeiras suffered their first defeat this year when they were hammered 5-2 by Corinthians, who left $4 million striker Tulio on the substitutes' bench. Palmeiras still lead group one of the competition while Corinthians are top of group two. The top two in each group go into a four-team play-off.
